title: Writing to Persuade Adventure
welcome_lead: Now apply the toolkit — write articles and speeches that actually convince people.
meta_desc: GCSE English Language transactional writing — AFOREST, structure, persuasive openings.
final_note: You practised structuring persuasive texts and using AFOREST to convince a reader.

walkthroughs.body_html: Remember AFOREST: Alliteration, Facts, Opinions, Rhetorical questions, Emotive language, Stats, Triplets.

Hook readers with a shocking statistic or rhetorical question.

End with a punchy call to action: 'Sign the petition. Today.'

Acknowledge the other side: 'Of course, some argue.' then dismantle it: '.but the evidence shows otherwise.'

This makes you sound fair AND right.

To whom it may
Greetings
Closing
Topic
Quote
Question
Overt prestige is loud speech and covert prestige is quiet speech.
By the word's grammatical function in a sentence — not its meaning. The same word can belong to different classes depending on use (e.g. 'run' as noun or verb).
A noun is always a person, place or thing.
A noun is any word that starts with a capital letter.
A semantic field is a field of study like physics or biology.
A group of words from a similar area of meaning — e.g. 'whisper, scream, mumble, shout' all belong to the semantic field of vocalisation.
A semantic field is a list of synonyms for one word.
A noun is any word that starts with a capital letter.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between overt and covert prestige?
options: Only standard language has prestige; non-standard varieties have none.
A noun is any word that starts with a capital letter.
Overt prestige is loud speech and covert prestige is quiet speech.

Overt prestige is the high status of standard varieties recognised by society (RP, Standard English); covert prestige is the hidden status of non-standard varieties within particular groups, signalling solidarity or toughness.
